findings.title: §9's SceneOverlay→Banners mapping drops H-2a-iii's visibility rule and maps a boolean onto a text field
findings.claim: §9 says `banner` maps to `banners.interior` and `layerPaused` to `banners.tactical`. But `layerPaused` is a boolean, and `banners.tactical` is `string | null`. H-2a-iii's scene also shows the interior banner in every view whenever the layer is not paused (`view === 'interior' || !overlay.layerPaused`). The online duel uses this to show its host-pause or disconnect banner over the map views too. §6 defines `banners.interior` as non-null only when `view === 'interior'`. An implementer who copies §6's rule into the scene would hide the online banner in Helm and Weapons.
findings.evidence: spec L355-357 (mapping), L267-268 (interior only in the interior view); helm-h2a-iii-online-app.md:L2288 (`layerPaused: boolean`), L2329 (`banner.visible = overlay.banner !== null && (view === 'interior' || !overlay.layerPaused)`), L2803 (online: `banner: bannerText(), layerPaused: false`)
findings.why: H-2a-iii's refinement will rebuild the scene from this mapping. As written, it loses the online duel's status banner in the map views, or two implementers will each invent their own condition.
findings.fix: State the mapping exactly: `banners.interior = overlay.banner !== null && (view === 'interior' || !overlay.layerPaused) ? overlay.banner : null`, and `banners.tactical = overlay.layerPaused ? pauseText : null`, where pauseText is the scene's `pauseText` option.

findings.title: The error boundary's reset rule ('until its slice is next cleared') has no meaning for the Menu region
findings.claim: §2 says a failed region renders nothing until its slice is next cleared. Hud, DuelUi and FlightUi each have a slice that their producer clears, but Menu has none. So if Menu throws once, it stays blank for the rest of the run. That also removes the strip's Leave and Pause, which this rule exists to protect. The spec also does not say how a boundary detects that its slice was cleared (for example, by a reset key taken from the slice's null-to-non-null transition).
findings.evidence: spec L144-146 (boundary rule, 'so a bad HUD model can never take away the strip's Leave and Pause'); L78 (Menu is gated on the mountUi prop, not on a slice); L92-93 (the menu slice is never cleared)
findings.why: Menu is the one region whose failure strands the player, and two implementers would reset its boundary differently, or not at all.
findings.fix: Give each boundary a reset key. For Hud, DuelUi and FlightUi, a counter bumped by the sink each time the slice goes from null to non-null. For Menu, `menu.page` together with `online.status?.phase`, so the next page change or status push retries it. Say that Menu's fallback still renders a minimal Leave/Return to menu control, or accept and document that it does not.

findings.title: §3 says SessionDeps.hud keeps its `{ update }` type, but §7 adds `clear()` to it
findings.claim: L183-184 says `SessionDeps.hud` keeps its `{ update(m: HudModel) }` type. §7 adds an optional `clear()` to the same dependency's type, and §1 requires every producer to clear on dispose.
findings.evidence: spec L183-184 vs L304-305 and L83
findings.why: This is a small contradiction that a UI-iii plan writer has to resolve on their own.
findings.fix: Change L183-184 to read `{ update(m: HudModel); clear?(): void }`.
